sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for report upload screen
sections.what: Brings in the drag and drop library, the upload hook, icons, and the card and button parts.
sections.why: Gives the uploader its drop area, its file list and its buttons.

sections.name: ReportUploader (part 1)
sections.title: Drop area and file picking rules
sections.what: Creates the large dashed box where users drop or click to choose files. It accepts PDF, JPG and PNG files up to 10 MB each. Files that are dropped are passed to the upload hook. Dragging over the box changes its color and wording.
sections.why: Limits uploads to document and photo types the system can read, and caps size to keep uploads manageable. Reason for the exact 10 MB limit is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The 10 MB limit and file types are set only in the browser, so the server must also check them. The text on the box says the files are HIPAA compliant, which this file cannot prove.

sections.name: ReportUploader (part 2)
sections.title: Upload queue list
sections.what: When files are waiting or in progress, shows a titled list of them, one row each, with a retry and remove action on each.
sections.why: Lets the user see each upload's progress and fix problems without losing other files.

sections.name: UploadItem (part 1)
sections.title: One upload row: status and progress
sections.what: Shows one file's name, size, a progress bar, and a status line. The bar and text change color and wording for error, processing, completed and uploading states. When the file is being processed, a spinning icon appears.
sections.why: Keeps the user informed while the system uploads the file and reads its contents.
sections.watch_out: The status line shows the stored error text directly, so error messages from the server reach the user as they are.

sections.name: UploadItem (part 2)
sections.title: Retry and remove buttons
sections.what: Shows a retry button only when an upload has failed, and a remove button on every row. These call the actions passed in from the list above.
sections.why: Lets the user try a failed upload again or remove a file from the queue.
sections.watch_out: Removing a row here may not cancel an upload already in progress. The code does not show this.

summary: The upload area on the reports page, where a patient drops or chooses PDF and image files, with a queue that shows each file's status.
purpose: Lets a patient add medical reports so their values can be read automatically.
why: Header says high-fidelity clinical document ingestion. The reasons for the file types and the 10 MB limit are not stated in the code.
how: Sets up a drop zone that accepts PDF, JPG, JPEG and PNG files up to 10 MB. Dropped files go to the addFiles function from the upload hook. Below, a queue lists each file with its name, size in MB, and a status bar. Each queue item has retry and remove actions. The visible part of the file ends partway through the queue item, so the status details are not fully shown.
inputs: Files dropped or chosen by the user, and the file list and actions from the upload hook.
outputs: Calls addFiles, retry and remove on the upload hook. Shows the queue and each file's status.
risks: The Take Photo button has no action in the visible code. The page says the upload is HIPAA compliant, but this file does not check that. Messages for rejected files are not shown in the visible code.
debug: If files are rejected, check the accepted types and the 10 MB limit. If the queue does not update, check the useUpload hook. Expect the Take Photo button to do nothing from this code alone.
